name: institutional-seed
description: Seed benchmark over the five synthetic institutional documents in evaluation/corpus/. Governed: questions and expected answers are fixed at this version and the dataset is immutable once loaded - a change means a new version, or last month's score and this month's describe different exams. NOT a substitute for a real institutional evaluation set: these documents are written for this benchmark, so a score here says the pipeline works, not that it works on your regulations. One answerable case (revaluation deadline) is a known miss at this baseline - see its notes. It is kept so that fixing it registers as an improvement rather than disappearing from the exam.

cases.question: What is the minimum attendance required to sit the end-semester examination?
cases.notes: Exact clause lookup. The baseline case: if this fails, retrieval is broken.

cases.question: Can a student with 60 percent attendance apply for condonation?
cases.expected_answer: No. Condonation below 65 percent is not permitted.
cases.notes: The answer is a negative stated in the document. A system that pattern-matches on 'condonation' without reading the bound gets this wrong.

cases.question: What is the tuition for B.Tech CSE?
cases.notes: Table row lookup. The figure is meaningless without its column header.

cases.question: What is the hostel fee for B.Tech MECH?
cases.notes: Different column, different row - catches an answer that returns the first row or the first number.

cases.question: How many books can a postgraduate student borrow?
cases.notes: Two limits in one clause. Returning 'four' is the failure to watch for.

cases.question: What is the late return fine for a library book?
What is the hostel curfew on Saturdays?
cases.notes: The clause states two curfews. A system that stops at the first returns 10 pm.

cases.question: What happens to a candidate caught using unauthorised material?
cases.expected_answer: Debarred from all examinations of that semester.

cases.question: When is the supplementary examination held?
What is the deadline for applying for revaluation?
cases.expected_answer: Within 15 days of the publication of results.
cases.notes: KNOWN MISS at the current baseline, kept deliberately. The answerer abstains: 'deadline' appears nowhere in the clause (it says 'within 15 days'), and no stemmer unifies 'applying' with 'application', so one query term of three matches - 0.33 coverage against a 0.34 floor. Retrieval finds the right document (recall@1 is 1.0); the extractive answerer will not quote from it. This is the lexical-matching limit the README documents, and it is exactly what a semantic embedding model would fix. Tuning the threshold to pass this one case would be fitting the system to the benchmark.

cases.question: What is the institute's policy on remote work for administrative staff?
cases.notes: Not in the corpus at all. A benchmark of only answerable questions cannot tell a well-calibrated system from one that never abstains - this is the case that scores calibration.

cases.question: What is the parking charge for visitors?
cases.notes: Plausible for an institution and absent from these documents. Shares vocabulary with the corpus ('visitors' appears in the hostel rules), so a system that abstains here is abstaining on substance rather than on vocabulary.

cases.question: Which faculty member chairs the examination committee?
cases.notes: The examination policy exists and does not name anyone. The nearest-miss case: the right document is retrievable and still contains no answer.
